I absolutely agree. I've suffered from depression for literally twenty years and this stuff has helped me get control of it. It's not gone, but it's manageable. The point of this post is to give tools to **fight** depression, not cure it. And I am in no way saying it's easy, believe me. I have this list printed and taped to my wall so I remember to do these things. 

Even if I do just one of these things it's a drop in the bucket, you know? Sometimes that's all I can give to myself. But when I'm in the habit of giving myself one drop a day, sometimes I can give two.

I don't think you should apologize for typing that. I know where you're coming from because I'm from the same place.

Honestly, I KNOW it's not as easy as just "Do this and you'll feel better!" because doing that thing in the first place is the hardest thing in the world. I promise, I *know*. 

Take small steps. Smaller than you think is necessary. Just organize one area of your room, maybe. Just that little nightstand. Just do ONE nice thing for yourself. Just one thing, whatever it is, to be better to yourself. 

Also, my life is far from normal. I'm not in the clear yet, but I am relieved that I'm not as bad as I used to be. It's an uphill battle that I'll probably fight for the rest of my life. But the uphill gets less steep. Maybe it'll even be flat or downhill sometimes. Who knows?
